question: Instead of flat method names, I want hierarchical structure like `client.admin.users.create()`. Does the order I specify groups matter? Will different languages automatically use their own naming style?
ground_truth: To configure nested method names, use the `x-fern-sdk-group-name` extension with multiple values as an array in your OpenAPI specification. For example, to create `client.admin.users.create()`, add `x-fern-sdk-group-name: [admin, users]` and `x-fern-sdk-method-name: create` to your endpoint definition. The order of group names matters - the SDK preserves the array order to build the hierarchy, so `[admin, users]` creates `client.admin.users` while `[users, admin]` would create `client.users.admin`. Importantly, the SDK generator automatically handles language-specific casing conventions: TypeScript will use `client.admin.users.create()` (camelCase), Python will use `client.admin.users.create()` (snake_case), and Go will use appropriate PascalCase. You define the logical grouping once, and Fern adapts it to each language's conventions, maintaining the hierarchy while respecting idiomatic naming patterns.

metadata.cited_context: If you add more than one `x-fern-sdk-group-name` extension, then the generated SDK will nest group names. The generated SDK method preserves the order of group names. In the example below, Fern will generate a method called `client.users.notifications.send()`: `x-fern-sdk-group-name: - users - notifications x-fern-sdk-method-name: send`
